summary: Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima, Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel, Khenchen Dazer, and Yonten Gonpo, later teaching numerous students.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche studied at Thrangu Monastery and under 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught at Rumtek Monastery (1959, 1967) and founded Karma Triyana Dharmachakra, serving as abbot in 1978.
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Bokar Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga. He taught students including Chatral Sangye Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Khenpo Shenga studied under Önpo Tenzin Norbu, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and others. He taught at Shri Singha Shedra (1902) and founded Dzongsar Monastery, becoming first khenpo of its shedra in 1918.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin and 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He served as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery (~1977) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (~1984–2004) and Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel. His students include Douglas S. Duckworth, Reb Gongwa Jamyang Chökyi Lodrö, and Ngak Sé Rigpé Dorjé.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under teachers including Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970) and at the University of Virginia (~1979–1980).

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, and others. He held teaching posts at Lhasa Mentsikhang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Active in Tibetology and other fields, Khyenrab Norbu studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen, later teaching Yeshi Dhonden and Byams-pa-phrin-las, among others.
Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ki-yong Rhi held positions at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Kiattisak Ponampon earned an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie. In 2013, he studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and other scholars.

A philosopher who studied at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo, and University of Freiburg, Ito held multiple academic positions at the University of Tokyo between 1911 and 1945, later serving at Hokkaido University (1947–1951) and Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott specializes in religious studies and Indology. She held a post at the University of Leeds (~1978–2012) and subsequently took a post at Lancaster University (~2012).

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, Plofker studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree. Her academic posts include MIT (2000–2004) and Union College, where she became an assistant professor in 2012 and associate professor in 2019.

Specializing in religious studies, Patton completed her dissertation at Harvard University, where she served as assistant professor (~1990). She was also an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens in 1991.

Active in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Tanaka earned degrees at the University of Tokyo, also studying at Oxford and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1985–1990) and the Eastern Institute.
